title: Incredibly P2W
body: I got this game and enjoyed it probably like most reviews on here that give it a good rating however, this review will actually give you what you need to know. First off this is a very good game in the first few hours. I will give them that it’s worth sinking some time in to. After a few days of doing all your quests and getting further on into the story a the dungeons and trials. You will hit brick walls at every single stage. Nearly impossible to complete walls without getting A. the perfect run where you get your exact upgrades at each shop visit OR B. Spend money to increase your backpack size. This is what I deemed fine because it’s a free game and really enjoyed the game so far. So I bought the little back pack upgrade for the rangers because I had just got the sniper unlocked. Here’s where the sunk cost fallacy might hit some people as I easily completed these next few things until I hit ANOTHER brick wall. Rangers cannot simply deal with the issues I’m dealing with. Okay. Another backpack upgrade and a few more $$ put into the game. Okay last time I spend money. Get through the stages. And it happens again. I basically need the $10 warrior back pack upgrade otherwise I cannot get past this story mission. I’ve spent days even getting perfect runs just attempting it across multiple characters but sorry I’m not spending nearly $30 just for a hero and or another backpack upgrade. You’re basically asking for a full on game at this point just to progress a couple story chapters or trial floors every couple days until we probably need to start paying for the event packages to get the best of the best stuff. With how much they obviously brick wall you in this game without having a choice but to spend money to advance even a single stage im just going to say this game is not worth it. Even with how enjoyable it is. I can just go play Tetris for free or another matching game with what this really boils down. Even with the fun I had I wish I could just get a refund and never have played this game.

title: Potentially Fun, for a Whale
body: GATHER ’ROUND, friends, for I have witnessed a MIRACLE of modern engineering! These fine developers have discovered how to make a man grateful for the privilege of having his pockets picked! Day one? They’ll shower you in diamonds! Pets! Gear! You’ll think you’ve found the golden goose! You’ll think SURELY this is the one—the gacha game that finally respects your time! Day three, friend. Day THREE. The diamonds dry up. Your build—your beautiful, carefully assembled (with zombie parts) build—gets hard-countered by a monster blocking your main progression route, as if by DIVINE DESIGN. Your backpack, that humble collection of slots you assumed was simply yours, reveals itself to be another paid option they’d rather you shell out for. And your only lifeline? A trickle of weekly missions that, if completed perfectly, might—might—fund a single pull or backpack upgrade. The cure costs ten-to-thirty dollars. Weekly. For a mobile game. Step right up and pay the man, or enjoy the world’s most elaborately constructed waiting room. Either way, somebody’s getting rich, and friend—it ain’t you.

You’ll have an extremely difficult time as a F2P player trying to get anything meaningful and worthwhile from doing all of your free event tasks. I personally paid for the permanent ad-free ticket, and while it does give a decent amount of currency and whatnot, I still feel like I’m constantly being pressured into buying MORE. It doesn’t feel good, and having all of that shoved into my face regularly makes me dislike the game overall despite it being such an enjoyable core gameplay experience. If you plan on getting into this, just know the game will hound you to death and back to buy in-game things with real money. It will feel terrible. If you can get past that, cool. title: Passion Product
body: I don’t normally write reviews, especially for games that I haven’t played for very long. That being said, I wanted to praise the developers for creating a game that is clearly as much a passion project as it is a product. A “passion product”, if you will. Don’t get me wrong, there is an obscene amount of in-app purchase options. And before long, I fully expect to hit a progression wall that can only be overcome by paying (at which point I’ll probably just delete the game - I refuse to play games where the only option is to pay to win). That being said, everything from the music to the spritework to the interactions between items all feels like it was “done with purpose”. Like the developers made it exactly how they wanted it to be rather than compromising quality or creative vision to ship a “finished” product sooner. In a gaming landscape dominated by corner-cutting triple-A messes, that care and attention to detail means a lot to me. As I said before, I haven’t been playing for long. But I still felt as though this game is worth reviewing, whether to inform other players or just to share my thoughts with the devs in the event that they read these. To people considering playing this game, give it a shot! To the devs, keep up the good work!

title: You get soft locked early
body: The game is pretty good, but what I don’t understand is the timer that it put during the battles. That basically ruins the game and makes it so that any other build that doesn’t produce DPS is basically obsolete. If you’re going to add a timer to a rogue like the you have to have a way to extend that time and not just lose basically due to only the time. Thats where the other problem comes in, you get soft locked early on and have to wait the day out to even have a chance to level up. Why put a cap amount on the daily dungeons and the put the extra try amounts behind a pay wall? Then all the f2p players are stuck waiting until the next day to level up their gear and try to produce enough DPS to kill an enemy rather than strategically making a backpack to counter an enemy, it just doesn’t make sense. I really like this game so I hope the devs don’t get greedy and lock up every opportunity to grow and level up behind a paywall because as of now I’m stuck waiting until the next day because I can’t produce enough damage to the enemies to kill them in time even with their dumb gimmicks that I think are cool, because of a stupid timer of just 30 seconds. title: A breath of fresh air
body: I’ll be honest, I came from a mobile ad on Block Blast thinking it would be nothing like the ad in classic mobile game style. I could not have been more wrong. This game genuinely feels like a labor of love. The events are fun, and the artwork and visuals are beautiful. Gameplay isn’t boring at all, it’s like skill-based resource management. There aren’t any paywalls, but it does offer in-app purchases for quick access to heroes or no ads, and when it DOES give ads, it’s on your own terms for things like free Hero Dungeon tickets to earn extra rewards. Even despite these boosts, getting good heroes and pets can be easy with some events, especially the latest one involving Bjorn, but I like having these options available. There are very often some major difficulty jumps, but it’s not super hard to get past them due to the leveling system of the game. There is also a bug where the music breaks and becomes this weird horror version of itself after certain ads, but a simple exiting and re-entering of the app fixes it quickly. I’ve practically fallen in love with this game, and hope to get access to my favorite hero Venom soon.

title: Fun Game, But Progression Hits a Wall
body: This game is really fun. The ads are completely optional and never pop up randomly, which I really appreciate. I’ve spent a lot of time unlocking characters and experimenting with different builds. In each chapter, you have to strategically collect the items you need to defeat bosses, and organizing your inventory so certain buffs work together feels like a fun puzzle. However, once you reach a certain point in the game, progression slows down significantly. When I hit a wall in the chapters, I naturally look toward dungeons and trials to level up my character and become stronger. The problem is that I end up hitting walls there as well. Eventually, the bosses in all three modes become so difficult that they feel nearly impossible to beat, leaving me stuck with no clear way to continue progressing. It becomes very difficult to advance without upgrading your equipment, and obtaining better gear takes ages. Adding a faster or more reliable way to earn gear could help with this issue. I’ve reached a point where some bosses, especially in dungeons, feel nearly impossible to beat. Since you don’t get much assistance in dungeons, the main way I’ve managed to clear difficult stages is by repeatedly rerolling the coin shop until I get the items I need. Making shop rerolls free in dungeons would help reduce the reliance on luck and make runs feel more strategic. Right now, it often feels like I’m restarting over and over just to find a specific item before I even have a chance of winning. Another idea could be adding an endless mode where players can keep pushing through waves or floors to earn coins and other rewards that help strengthen their characters. It would give players another way to progress when they hit a wall in the main content and provide a fun long term goal outside of chapters, dungeons, and trials. Overall, this is a really cool game with a lot of fun mechanics, but the progression eventually slows down so much that it can feel frustrating and almost impossible to continue advancing. Hopefully as the game updates these issues are resolved.
